newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aubry defends French child benefit reform.
newsitem.headline: Aubry defends French child benefit reform.

text.p: French Employment Minister Martine Aubry said on Tuesday the family benefits system faced a deficit of 10 billion francs this year and this justified reform in the name of greater solidarity.

She was referring to proposals announced by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin in his June 19 debut parliamentary speech to limit some child benefits to households with monthly revenue of less than 25,000 francs.
The proposal has provoked an outcry from some family lobbies and Aubry declined to refer to the specifics of the proposals, sticking to a line that "we are continuing consultations".
Those who have attacked the plan have seized on election pledges by the left to increase consultation before acting.
Aubry said the existing system tended to redistribute money "more in the direction of poorer to richer families".
Reform on the family benefits side would not be applied in the other two areas of a heavily strained social security system, retirement and sickness cover, she stressed.
"We'd never apply the same logic to health and retirement, which are insurance systems and are not to be subjected to an income-test regime," she said.
Aubry also said the idea of reducing tax relief for people employing household staff, such as home childcare staff, would not be an urgent issue.
